about: Where the TF2 Voice Emulator stands. Read CLAUDE.md first, then this. The orchestrating session keeps this file; builders do not edit it. Since 2026-11-12 it holds where things stand now. What it no longer carries (each stand's history, the decisions no longer in force, the list of merges) is in docs/PROGRESS-LOG.md, dated and appended to, never edited; docs/README.md indexes every order with its state.

live.serves: main (GitHub Pages from the branch root)
live.main: the head of main (git log); the site's cache number is below
live.last_merge: AC-02 (no cache change, 2026-11-14): the accuracy suite's --seeds n measures each row at n different seeds (its own or the default, then the first n - 1 others from seed 1) and prints each figure as a median with its range, the worst band as the median seed's by size; without the option the suite is unchanged; tests/retiming.mjs refuses seeded JSON. Before it: AC-01 (no cache change, 2026-11-14): the accuracy suite renders each take as the page does by default, Steam voice on the game's voice queue (300 frames a second, voice_buffer_ms 100; Set C's photographed 295 and 336); with loss or jitter on the queue the render is lined up as the take is (the review's finding); the predictions keep the file's own timing; tests/retiming.mjs refuses JSON rendered on the queue; music_take_it_off's cut ends before the take's key release. docs/ACCURACY.md's table is the suite on the queue (private run, measured).

waiting_on_the_owner: The run sheet of 2026-11-11 (private repository; given to the owner): blocks 1 and 2 bad connections on one PC (35 min), 3 Steam's voice settings (20), 4 speakers and Sound quality (15), 5 two talkers and 6 one-way loss with the second PC (55); with the Miles run (the older engine files arrived 2026-11-11).

Not urgent: the live monitor's box "the game's voice queue" (W3-02c-3, merged 2026-11-14) is off on every load. With it on the monitor is about 102 ms later at 66.67 frames a second and 357 ms later at 300 than with it off (read), and each phrase waits as the game's does. Say if it should be on by default instead.

Optional, for the receiver's queue: one take of several minutes of steady sound (no pauses) at fps_max 67 with the channel's log on, to see whether a long unbroken phrase really reaches the queue's fade and underruns as the read rules predict (after 1.3 to 2.8 minutes at 67 fps).
W3-11c's key run (docs/work-orders/W3-11-steam-gate.md, 'The run'; docs/owner-runs.md): six cases with Steam's and the game's console logs, two tones, the uptimes. Nothing else waits for it.

Not urgent, new 2026-11-13: one take of the modern path that could be published. Every Steam take in the record carries the owner's voice, so none can go out. A clip made by a script of ours, fed through Steam's mic_inputfile, with voice_recordtofile 1 and voice_maxgain 1 in the game, would give the game's decoded voice of a signal anyone can regenerate. The procedure is written into docs/owner-runs.md by RP-01's part e.

Not urgent, new 2026-11-14: in the same session as the run sheet's queue block, two short stretches at fps_max 30 and 20 with voice_showchannels 2 (docs/owner-runs.md, 'The queue at low frame rates'), for W3-23's check against the game.
open_questions: Steam's sender: the 8-step (250 ms) pattern of chunk ends, which createClock lacks (Set D's demo, Set L).

The device stage's last unit: a single-precision read position and a loss of up to one unit toward zero before the last rounding (the retake R1-3). Cheaper than a read of the XAudio2 module: the same take at volume 1 with a voice that stays off the clamp.

Speex beyond the game's setting: only engine quality 3 (20-byte frames) was read and run with care; the other qualities use other codebooks and quantisers. The lost-frame and sub-mode 0 paths draw noise from the C runtime's rand() of the game's thread and cannot be reproduced from packets.

Set D, PC A with set_d_street: measured again 2026-11-14 on the stretches both pick, with the take lined up on the render's timeline, over nine seeds of the room: at 68.02 ms the render 0.0279 to 0.0300 against the take's 0.0257 (scatter 0.0024), 9 to 17% high, 0.9 to 1.8 scatters; 120.04 ms 0.0115 to 0.0138 against 0.0141; 308.02 ms 0.0071 to 0.0098 against 0.0056. The 36% of W3-17c's run came from each file's own stretches. What is left at 68 ms is within 2 scatters and not looked into further.

2026-11-12, from the structure audit: the capture's roll-off filter (captureEq, a 255-tap fit to one PC's measured roll-off) and the app's own resampler in front of Steam's sender are the last fitted stages on the modern preset's path, and no order replaces them. By the finish line they need a measurement (what Windows hands Steam at 24 kHz) or a stated reason.

The weak takes of the accuracy run of 2026-11-12, checked against the record at the documents' review: each is explained (docs/ACCURACY.md). The default take's blocks are those of findings 13 and 14; the two low-tone takes differ block by block because their comfort noise is random in take and render (finding 18); the second PC's take ran at settings fitted before that PC's were inferred, and at the inferred ones (volume 0.11, voice_scale 0.77; the accuracy manifest since 2026-11-12) it reads 0.959 where it read 0.838. What stays open: that take's +0.5 dB overall and +2.4 dB at 11 to 12 kHz, its settings read off that PC, and the render's 1.7 to 2.3 points more samples at the clamp than three lossless takes.
The wet retake R3-3 placed to the sample (the fully wet room take fits the module with a residual 37 to 43 dB under it in its best seconds).

When phrases start, after the investigation of 2026-11-13 (docs/reports/W3-02c2-render-channel.md): the channel's clock gives the logged queue on the game's own packets (median difference 0.0 ms) and is not in question. Open in the sender's model: (1) the capture phase, which has an order (next); (2) the speech take's third transition, where the model leaves out 68 ms more than the take did (265 against 197 ms in the median) and the fourth and fifth follow from it; neither the phase nor the capture's level explains it, and how long Steam had run moves it; (3) the model opens on six frames in 17% of openings where the game did in 2 of 49. What would settle them: Steam's per-chunk console with the speech source playing, the queue's log on the listener, and Steam's uptime noted; for which pause appends in Set D, a queue log on the listening PC beside the demo.
The gain at 44.1 kHz on Steam voice has no sample-exact check against the game (Set J was made at voice_maxgain 1, where the gain is unity).
Steam's 16-bit decode past full scale (nothing in Set J passed it) and libopus 1.1.4 against 1.1.5 are not told apart.
On a 44100 Hz listener's device there is no roll-off (inferred from the read, no take).
For a later clock order: capture steps readable on a 10 ms tick, and the constant capture phase taken out of the tick (W3-16's second read).
The rooms: the tail's decay cannot be read from any take so far; why Set B is dry is not explained; Set D's PC B has a 140 ms echo that is not explained.

Miles (not in TF2), after the 2006 sitting of 2026-11-13 (codec 143,796 of 145,800 samples equal): why the first frames after a silence of 0.5 s or more are up to 32 steps off (the public implementation, or the opening block the module does not set); why the receiver's codec is reset twice before a second press; the exact decoder; what a lost frame sounded like; those engines' mixer and output.

Bad connections: the combined take has more silence than the rule; a 340 ms stretch of generated sound past ten frames; Steam's concealment against the bundled library's; after BC-1 the speech_loss10 row's +0.5 dB and two frame-log flaws under jitter and loss together.
A registered prediction for vaudio_celt_high (P2's hypotheses were registered with settings the engine never selects).
W2-03: whether a source longer than AUTO_RENDER_SECONDS should still render by itself when it is loaded (the owner's).

From the private runs of 2026-11-13 on a render that runs the queue: the level in half-second blocks of the speech take against a 'game' render at 300 frames a second is 0.29 to 2.81 dB rms over seven seeds (1.01 against the default render) and is not lowest where the fewest phrases moved; not explained. The gain is set back to 1.0 at each channel opened (read), so where channels open moves the level; whether that is all of it is not checked.

From the private runs of 2026-11-13 on a render that runs the queue, under loss at 15%: a 'game' render at 300 frames a second has 16.4% silent time in the mean of five seeds (7.3 to 25.8) where the one take has 10.1% and the default render 10.2%; its jumps across a lost run are of the take's kind (220 ms and more) with 1 to 11 a seed of 60 to 220 ms where the take has 1. Whether the game hands a refused message to the channel as an empty packet is still not read (BC-3, block 1).

2026-11-13: finding 23's 104 ms dropped at a channel's opening is a floor: a log replayed counts the least that can have dropped. Counted alike, renders and logs agree (96.4 to 103.2 ms against 98.9 to 102.2, measured); the renders' true figure is 113 to 126 ms, so the game's is likely 15 to 20 ms above 104 too (inferred). During the wait itself the game drops 10 to 17 ms more than a render (measured; two causes named, neither tested).

2026-11-13, from W3-21's build: the arrival figure of 50.5 ms (ARRIVAL_SECONDS in voice-channel.js, the time from a packet's last sample to its arrival, by which a 'game' render is lined up with its source) was fitted on seeds 1 to 50. On seeds 1 to 200 the timeline's zero is +2.7 ms off and on seeds 201 to 400 +1.0 ms (measured by the builder on main's behaviour; the spurts of one seed are not independent, so the suite's standard error understates the spread). A few milliseconds are under what any take resolves. To do: measure it again over many seeds with a standard error taken by seed; a small order of its own.

2026-11-13, from the private runs after W3-21: at the ten changes around the 420 and 440 ms pauses of Set D's sender take a 'game' render at 300 frames a second has the take's kind of change in 114 of 300 seed-changes with the drawn capture phase, 107 before it and 121 with the phase held at the demo's own 318 samples (measured). The capture's phase is therefore a small part of that shortfall; what makes the render's queue run out sooner than the take's after such a pause is not explained. At 240 ms pauses the render has the take's kind in 327 of 360 (291 before).

Where each overflow cut falls inside a sound at 300 frames a second is the model's (W3-02d-1's second read: nine cuts in the first 17.3 s of unbroken sound on the page's draw). The game's logs give what a restart drops (55 to 136 ms, finding 23) and the takes show skips after a restart, but no take was lined up cut for cut against a render on the game's queue.

2026-11-14: the level figure of a Steam row moves with the draw of the sender, the room and the loss (measured over nine seeds since AC-02; docs/ACCURACY.md's table gives the median and range): take4_my_own_speech 2.28 dB (0.18 to 3.07), sender_A 0.80 (0.10 to 1.10), net_baseline 0.38 (0.24 to 2.18); the model against its own render reads 0.27 to 0.80 on the network test signal. What a take can be expected to read is bounded by that spread.

model.where: tests/REFERENCE_2026.md, "Model", has every stage with what the game does, what the app runs and the basis; docs/ACCURACY.md states it stage by stage for readers.
model.capture: The left channel of a stereo file, resampled to 24 kHz; the capture roll-off a 255-tap filter fitted to the owner's PC; on steam rounded to 16 bits before the sender.
model.sender: steam: Steam's sender as read (the chunk rule, 2400 samples of pre-roll, the 0.4 s hold on a 32-bit float clock of Steam's uptime, 9 days by default); when Steam reads its microphone is a seeded model fitted to its packets. steam_48 (not in TF2): the 20 ms frame gate, a fit. The engine codecs: no gate unless voice_vad 1.
model.codec: steam: libopus 1.1.5 at Steam's settings, the 16-bit decode, at most 10 frames concealed; Steam's recording in 524,286 of 524,288 samples (Set J). celt_22, celt_44: the game's CELT 0.11 build, Set H's recordings but for 1 and 75 samples one step off. speex: Speex 1.0.2 with the module's arithmetic, equal to Sets M and O. miles (not in TF2): VR12, not checked against any recording of a running engine.
model.network: steam: a lost packet takes its whole message (BC-1, v33). Jitter on every profile is the earlier fit (3.2% of frames late at 50 ms); the game makes no frame late, and BC-4 is not built. The frame profiles: loss in bursts, the earlier fit.
model.receiver: steam: FFmpeg's resampler as ported, the fma3 kernel. The gain is the engine's rule, sample for sample on Set H, on the decoder's own stream for the engine codecs since W3-19 (v30). The voice channel is not in a render: a render keeps the source's timeline. The channel module is built as read (W3-02c-1, merged 2026-11-12) and no render runs it yet.
model.mixer_output: The engine's mixer and output stage as read, in integers (W3-10); the device stage to 48000 Hz a measured model; volume 1, the game's own.
model.rooms: The rooms are the engine's, in the render (W3-17c, v28), on the page and in the live chain (W3-17d, v31); the default is no room.
model.live: steam's live chain is the render sample for sample (W3-11b); push-to-talk is the app's stand-in until W3-11c.

finish_line: 2026-11-12, agreed with the owner: two tracks. The tool has a finish line: every stage of the modern preset (the steam profile at its defaults) is either equal to a take sample for sample or has its remaining difference measured and explained. By it the last builds are the receiver's queue (W3-02c-2, c-3, d) and jitter as arrival delays (BC-4); the open measurements (speech_loss10's +0.5 dB after BC-1, Set D's 68 ms echo, whether a long unbroken phrase reaches the queue's fade) stand between built and finished. The research track (the older codecs beyond what TF2 runs, Miles, bad connections in depth) has no finish line; it is done for its interest and is queued after the tool's line, not ahead of it. Findings are dated to the files they were read from (a Steam update can change them) and rest on one PC apart from the two-PC set; the findings document says how each could be checked elsewhere. Agreed the same day as the plan after the line: finish the two builds, write the findings document, then add no further codec; get one finding checked on someone else's PC (the hold against Steam's uptime is the plainest); after that the project's worth to others is in being readable, so the documentation and structure pass ranks above another codec. The documents state prominently what is not exact, phrase timing first (47% of transitions and a start error of 122 ms on the speech take; part of it cannot be closed, since the sender's clock phase is not in a recording). A search of 2026-11-12 for earlier public work found the packet format (Zhenyang Li, 2021, and tools built on it) and a CELT demo decoder that calls the game's library, and nothing on the sender's gate, hold or clock, the receiver's gain, queue or mixer, or Steam's uptime; a dozen queries prove no absence. Added 2026-11-13 after W3-02c-3 was planned again: W3-02c-3 is the last build the line's list names, and the line's measurement does not wait for it, since it closes no stage against a take. Added 2026-11-14: Set D's 68 ms echo was measured again on matched stretches (9 to 17% high over nine seeds, within 2 scatters; docs/ACCURACY.md, Rooms), and the accuracy suite renders on the game's voice queue since AC-01. Added 2026-11-14 after AC-02: speech_loss10's +0.5 dB reads +0.1 in the median of nine draws on the game's voice queue (-0.0 to +0.4; measured); of the line's open measurements, the long unbroken phrase (the owner's take at fps_max 67) remains.
takes: Since 2026-11-09 the owner's takes are in a private repository a session can attach (the owner knows its name; it is not named here). It holds Sets A to F as FLAC, the Set D demo, the source speech and clip, and the three test signals as played; the checksums of the Set D and F files match tests/REFERENCE_2026.md. The two songs played for Set A are there too. Not found: take1_default.flac (only the voice_maxgain 10 take of that pair; the tests accept either). The six prediction takes are not recorded yet. tests/accuracy.mjs and tests/retiming.mjs can run wherever that repository is cloned: pass its folder with --takes, and copy its signals folder into tests/testsignal/ (ignored by git). Published since RP-01e (2026-11-13, on the owner's word): the seven recordings of Sets H, I, M and O that tests/recordings/manifest.json lists, under tests/recordings/files/; the manifest is the list. Everything else of the takes stays private.
ci: Since S3-01b (2026-11-12) the workflow runs five jobs side by side (units, engine, render, stages, browser), each with 20 minutes, and a sixth, verify, that succeeds only if all five did: the one result to read on a head is verify with the conclusion success (a run cancelled by a newer push leaves it skipped, which is not a pass). A push has its result about five minutes later. A commit is tested once, on its push; a push that changes nothing outside docs/ runs nothing; a newer push to a branch cancels the older run, except on main, where every push runs to its end. On a push to main the units job also runs tests/cache-number.mjs against the commit main was at before the push, and fails if a file the site keeps offline changed without the cache number rising. The two browser checks that failed by timing ([Browser 3e], [Browser 10]) were repaired in S3-01b, so a red run is a real failure. If Ubuntu's package mirrors cannot be reached the browser job runs on the runner image's own libraries and says so in a warning. The history of CI's limits and outages is in docs/PROGRESS-LOG.md.
priority: The owner cares most about the modern preset (the Steam profile at defaults), which they have A/B tested against the game. Work on it comes before the legacy codecs and the rooms.

decisions_in_force.what: The first target for long sources is 30 minutes at 48 kHz for audio and video files (a sample budget, so 15 minutes at 96 kHz), the whole voice of a demo up to 60 minutes, and 30 minutes for a recording. Where the browser reports under 8 GB of device memory, the budget stays at 10 minutes.
decisions_in_force.why: After the render and the meter stream, loading the file is the peak (about 4.5 float copies of it), which a desktop tab can hold for 30 minutes and a phone cannot. The owner can overrule any of these numbers; they are constants in app/core.js (W2-03).

decisions_in_force.what: Sources up to 10 minutes keep process() until the stream has proved itself; then one path.
decisions_in_force.why: The registered predictions and every test depend on today's renders. W2-02 records golden hashes so the switch can be shown to change nothing.

decisions_in_force.what: The owner's standard is an exact recreation by any means. The orchestrator will not use leaked engine source; the owner supplied their own install's engine and codec files and the game's 'find voice' output, and reading those is allowed (CLAUDE.md, hard rules).
decisions_in_force.why: The receiver's queue and the legacy codecs' settings are in those files, and the public SDK has neither.

decisions_in_force.what: From the receiver plan (docs/reports/W3-02-plan.md): on the page the modern preset will render the game's timeline by default (fps_max 300, voice_buffer_ms 100) with the source's timeline one setting away; a video source and the engine's own default (process() with no option) keep the source's timeline; the flat 41% rule is retired when that lands. The queue test's fixture built from the owner's logs stays in the private repository; the public suite runs a synthetic log and the orchestrator runs the private replay.
decisions_in_force.why: The owner's standard is what the game does, and the queue is now the engine's rule, confirmed on every tick of the logs and by the frame-rate test. Sound leading the picture by up to 0.35 s would be worse than the timing it fixes. The fixture shows when the owner was speaking; nothing is lost by keeping it private.

decisions_in_force: 2026-11-10, the owner on shipping a modified LGPL file (the resampler port, W3-13): 'Regarding a license stuff, do what you think is best.' The orchestrator's choice: ship it, as recommended (LAME is already shipped under the LGPL; the port keeps its notices, carries the licence text and a dated notice of change, and is its own source). Licence questions of this kind are the orchestrator's to decide from now on, said plainly to the owner when one is decided.

2026-11-10, rooms. The owner, asked about the default place of the listener, the custom room and the preset numbers: "With your questions for me. Do what you think is best." Decided by the orchestrator: the default stays no room, named for what it is in the game (Sound quality: Low, dsp_slow_cpu 1), with the room of Set C as the first choice under it, until a fully wet take matches sample for sample; then the default is looked at again. The custom room stays as an extra, rebuilt on the engine's processors. The parameters of the automatic room's 16 templates go into the repository as numbers, as presets 0 to 29 already are; the game file's text does not. The owner does not recall changing Sound quality between Set B and the later sets (about two months ago).

2026-11-10, scope. The orchestrator's proposal: aim for a defined 1.0 (the modern preset on Steam's real path for file and live microphone, the output stage, the game's rooms in the render and on the page, every setting labelled by its evidence), build only the deterministic rules of the receiver's work and leave re-timing and loss labelled experimental, and put later findings on a list built only if audible or nearly free. The owner: "It's mainly for me. But I agree that the pages clarity, defaults, and speed are important too. I think the fidelity of the main modern preset is basically indistinguishable to the real thing". So: the 1.0 list stands; the page's clarity, defaults and speed become a piece of work of their own (an audit and an order, W4-01); the receiver's orders shrink as proposed when their turn comes.

2026-11-10, the page. After the page audit (docs/reports/W4-01-page-audit.md), the owner: clips are usually music and often over a minute ("Yes. I usually put in music"), so the first seconds playable while the rest renders is built (W4-01b step 3) and parallel workers are left out; the developer console's simulated chat feed keeps its name list ("Keep it"); the default for volume becomes the game's own, 1.0, with a label that says so ("1.0 with the label"), the change made by W3-10 since it re-records every hash. Music keeps the gate open for the whole clip, so for the owner's use the codec, the gain, the output stage and the rooms matter most.

2026-11-10, priority. The owner, on the page order against the rest: "Stuff that has to do with audio processing is more important to me". So nothing of W4-01 moves ahead of audio work. The sequence: W3-11b (being built), W3-10 (the output stage), W3-17c (the rooms in the render), W3-17d (the room panel, which the rooms need to be usable, with W4-01d's words), then W4-01a and c, then W4-01b (speed). The owner's own use is mostly music, for which the codec, the gain, the output stage and the rooms decide the sound.

2026-11-11, two rules changed by the owner: "Yeah run game files if you can. Remove the audible only standard". (1) The owner's game modules may be run inside a CPU emulator (no Wine, no Windows, no network; CLAUDE.md has the wording), which gives reference output for any input. (2) The standard of 2026-11-11 (audible only) is withdrawn the same day: exactness is pursued again where it can be had, so the three items it parked are back in the queue as investigations (the device stage's last unit, with a read and if useful an emulated run of the sound device module; the 250 ms pattern of Steam's capture; the wet retake R3-3 to the sample). Usage still paces the work: one builder and one investigator at a time.

2026-11-11, widened the same hour. The owner: "Yes, game files means any file. Also, it doesn't have to be emulator only. Use whatever tools and means that you deem as necessary and useful". So Steam's and Windows' files of the owner's install are covered as the game's are, and Wine or a like tool is allowed where an emulator falls short (CLAUDE.md has the wording, with our own precaution: no network, away from credentials). Unchanged: no leaked source, and the owner's recordings and personal details stay private. Also from the owner that night: "Do what you think is best. Don't let me block you", so the order of work and open offers (the footer's version line goes into W3-17d) are decided without asking.

2026-11-11, Miles, three rulings. Asked whether the candidate's tables may be in the repository, whether the decoder is to be exact or within one step, and what the encoder starts from, the owner: "for these questions, I'm leaving it up to your discretion. you're the expert". The orchestrator's rulings: (1) the candidate is vendored as third-party code under its licence in a folder of its own, with our README on where it comes from; only its three source files and licence are taken (CLAUDE.md has the rule); (2) within one step now, an exact decoder as a later order; (3) the encoder starts from one block of zeros, stated as a choice. The build is split: W3-20a the codec and the game's wrapper as a module with tests against the vectors measured from the owner's plug-in; W3-20b the profile, after the older engine files show what rate an engine gave the codec. Each ruling is the owner's to reverse.

2026-11-11, W3-20b's eight open points (the Miles questions are the orchestrator's by the owner's delegation): the order's recommendations taken as written; each is the owner's to reverse. The profile is listed under 'Not in Team Fortress 2' on the page, per the owner's instruction that Miles be marked as not a TF2 codec.

2026-11-11, the owner on the render's name. Asked whether the switch beside the player would say 'TF2 voice' for a render made with vaudio_miles, the owner chose one neutral label for every codec ('Yeah I think a neutral label might be better'). So the page says 'Hear: Rendered | Original', 'RENDER' and 'ORIGINAL' on the views and the loudness table, and 'the render' in sentences; the codec's own name, with 'not in TF2' or 'not in the game' where that holds, is in the status line under the player.

2026-11-12, the owner on the documents: "yeah lets do a full pass of all documentation/readme stuff" and "feel free to fully rewrite whatever you feel is best, with whatever scope. the documentation and readme has been carried over for probably about half a year or so now, and a lot of work has been done since".

2026-11-12, the owner, widening the pass: "that last message I sent also goes for the general structure and operation of the entire project"; the project is about a year old, stalled before the current models, and its structure and documents were carried over from then. Structure may be rewritten freely; the orchestrator's line: a change of structure moves no recorded hash, and one that would is an accuracy order and needs a measurement.

2026-11-12, the owner: "Steer this however you see fit. I'm an irrational, emotional, dopamine-driven human. So take my momentary leanings with a grain of salt." So a passing interest of the owner's is weighed, not followed as a re-ordering; an explicit request still is one. The exact Miles decoder stays on the research track, after the tool's finish line.

2026-11-12, the orchestrator, with S3-01b: the cache number in sw.js is set at the merge by the orchestrator (node tests/cache-number.mjs origin/main, with --set when it says a cached file changed) and never by a builder. A line in an order written before this that says "CACHE up by one" is void; the order's brief says so. A builder still changes sw.js's list when its change adds, removes or renames a file the site loads.

2026-11-12, the owner, asked whether the game's recordings of the project's own synthetic test signal may be published (sound only: no speech, music, console log, demo or packet dump): "Do what you think is best". The orchestrator's ruling: yes, for those files only, and only through the order that builds the reproduce-it page. That order names each file, shows that its source is the synthetic signal and nothing of the owner's voice or music, strips and checks its metadata, decides where the files live (release assets or the repository, by size), amends the hard rule in CLAUDE.md in the same change, and the orchestrator reads every file's header before the push. Until that order is merged the rule stands as written and nothing of the takes is published. Publishing cannot be undone, so a doubt about a file leaves it out.
